title: A chloride–bicarbonate product fails a cross-sample incremental systolic-pressure prediction test
abstract: Serum chloride–bicarbonate interaction did not establish incremental systolic-pressure prediction beyond flexible routine measures across NHANES2011–2012 and2013–2014: MSE gain 0.277878mmHg² (0.138%), source-targetPSU refit95% interval [-1.025016,0.931664]. A fixed source-trained weighted ridge model was transferred without target fitting from 4268 to 4653 complete-case adults. Target MSE changed 201.011362 to 200.733484mmHg². Unweighted analysis and source-percentile clipping reversed the small point gain. This is a negative incremental-model result, not equivalence, a novel acid-base mechanism, or a clinical diagnostic claim.

citations.reason: Serum anion gap and blood pressure in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2007); prior cross-sectional acid-base/BP association motivating the question, not proof of incremental prediction.
Serum chloride is an independent predictor of mortality in hypertensive patients (2013); motivating context only, not an outcome replicated here.
